scenario: AITA for being home all day and refusing to cook for my mom? | I'm a female in my senior year of high school and I have a younger sister in grade 10. As most of you know, schools have been closed for a while now and won't reopen for at least another month. My dad gets to work from home, but my mom still has to go out to her office. My school just started online teaching, and we've been getting a lot of assignments to complete. However, my mom expects us to make dinner basically every night because "we're home all day". That really annoyed me because yeah "we're home all day" but we have school work to do. I got upset and asked her why doesn't she cook, since she always finishes work at 5 pm and her office is like 6 minutes from home. Well, once she got home today and saw there was no dinner prepared, she got pissed and started screaming at me how she's so ashamed of us and how we're useless. When I explained how yes we're home all day but doesn't mean we have the whole day off, she got even more mad and said that it doesn't take that long to cook. I refuted by "why don't you cook then?" For more context, my mom is an awful cook. She literally puts no effort into learning or looking up recipes. My dad is an excellent cook. He's tried to teach her before, but she refuses to learn and complains. Before, he would cook for us almost every day, even if he came home late from work (he has a high demanding job so his hours range but he's home 6 pm the EARLIEST, sometimes as late as 9 or even 10 pm. + 30-40 minutes one way commuting). And what does he come home to? Either a low effort flavourless meal from my mom, or my mom sitting on her ass watching TV and asking him what's he's gonna make for dinner. So my dad is forced to make dinner at a late hour so he can eat. More recently, he would just eat fast-food before coming home because he doesn't expect dinner to be on the table. However, he asks if us girls are hungry and offers to cook something for us to eat because he's worried that our mom didn't make us a proper meal. I'm a good cook too (self taught), and I try to help out if I don't have too much homework to do. So AITA for not cooking dinner today and telling my mom to not expect dinner every time she comes home? Also, my dad ended cooking in the end today.

### A Step‑by‑Step Plan for Your First Turkey Below is a practical, “cook‑like” roadmap that covers everything from thawing to carving. Feel free to tweak any step to match your family’s exact recipe or traditions. | Day | What to Do | Why It Matters | |-----|------------|----------------| | **Day‑1 (If frozen)** | **Thaw** the turkey in the refrigerator (24 h per 4–5 lb). | Keeps the bird safe and prevents uneven cooking. | | **Day‑1** | **Prep the brine** (if you’re using one). | Adds moisture and flavor. | | **Day‑1** | **Gather all ingredients** (herbs, butter, spices, stuffing, etc.). | Avoid last‑minute scrambling. | | **Day‑1** | **Clean the kitchen** (wash all surfaces, prep a clean roasting pan). | Hygiene is key for a safe meal. | | **Day‑2 (Morning)** | **Brine the turkey** (or rinse & pat dry if you skip brine). | Brine time: 12–24 h in the fridge. | | **Day‑2 (Evening)** | **Season the turkey** (rub, salt, pepper, herbs, butter, etc.). | Builds flavor; let it sit at room temp 30–60 min before roasting. | | **Day‑3 (Morning)** | **Preheat the oven** to 325 °F (165 °C). | Consistent heat gives even cooking. | | **Day‑3 (Morning)** | **Place turkey on a rack** in a roasting pan. | Allows air circulation for crisp skin. | | **Day‑3 (Morning)** | **Add a drip pan** (water, broth, or apple juice). | Keeps the pan clean and adds moisture to the oven. | | **Day‑3 (Morning)** | **Roast** (see timing table below). | Core of the process. | | **Day‑3 (Late)** | **Rest the turkey** for 20–30 min. | Juices redistribute; easier carving. | | **Day‑3 (Evening)** | **Carve & serve**. | The moment of pride! | --- ## 1. Thawing & Brining | Step | Details | |------|---------| | **Thaw** | 4–5 lb per 24 h in the fridge. If you’re short on time, use the cold‑water method (submerge in cold water, change every 30 min). | | **Brine (optional)** | Classic: 1 cup kosher salt + ½ cup brown sugar + 1 lb turkey + water (enough to cover). Add aromatics (bay leaves, peppercorns, garlic, herbs). Chill 12–24 h. | | **Rinse & Pat Dry** | After brining, rinse under cold water, pat dry with paper towels. | > **Tip:** If you skip brine, you can still keep the bird moist by basting with butter or pan juices every 45 min. --- ## 2. Seasoning & Flavor | Ingredient | Typical Use | |------------|-------------| | **Salt & Pepper** | Basic seasoning; use kosher or sea salt. | | **Herbs** | Thyme, rosemary, sage, parsley. Mix with butter or olive oil. | | **Garlic** | Minced or whole cloves tucked under skin. | | **Butter** | Softened, mixed with herbs; rub under skin for extra moisture. | | **Stuffing** | If you’re stuffing the bird, use a dry, well‑seasoned mix. Keep stuffing separate if you’re worried about food safety. | > **Family‑Recipe Hook:** If your family’s recipe calls for a specific herb blend or a special glaze, incorporate it at the seasoning stage. Write it down or print it out so you don’t forget any detail. --- ## 3. Roasting ### Oven Temperature & Timing | Weight | Approx. Time (at 325 °F) | Internal Temp Goal | |--------|--------------------------|--------------------| | 8–12 lb | 2 h 30 min – 3 h | 165 °F (breast) | | 12–14 lb | 3 h – 3 h 30 min | 165 °F (breast) | | 14–18 lb | 3 h 30 min – 4 h | 165 °F (breast) | > **Rule of Thumb:** 13 min per pound is a good baseline, but always check the thermometer. ### Steps 1. **Place the turkey breast‑side up** on a rack in a roasting pan. 2. **Add a drip pan** (water, broth, or apple juice) to catch juices and keep the pan clean. 3. **Roast** uncovered. If the skin browns too fast, tent with foil. 4. **Baste** every 45 min with melted butter or pan juices (optional but adds flavor). 5. **Check internal temp** with a probe thermometer: - **Breast**: 165 °F - **Thigh**: 175 °F - **Stuffing** (if inside): 165 °F > **Safety Note:** The USDA recommends 165 °F for poultry. If you’re stuffing the bird, the stuffing must reach 165 °F as well. --- ## 4. Resting - **20–30 min** on a cutting board, tented loosely with foil. - Resting lets juices redistribute, making the meat juicy and easier to carve. --- ## 5. Carving 1. **Remove the legs & thighs** first. Slice the joint and separate the drumstick. 2. **Slice the breast**: cut from the breastbone outward, then slice each breast piece. 3. **Serve** immediately, or keep warm in a low‑heat oven (200 °F) while you finish carving. --- ## 6. Timing Checklist (for a 12‑lb turkey) | Time | Action | |------|--------| | **Day‑1** | Thaw, brine, prep ingredients | | **Day‑2** | Season, let sit 30 min | | **Day‑3 6 am** | Preheat oven, set up pan | | **Day‑3 6:30 am** | Put turkey in oven | | **Day‑3 9:00 am** | First basting | | **Day‑3 10:30 am** | Second basting | | **Day‑3 12:00 pm** | Check temp; if done, remove | | **Day‑3 12:15 pm** | Rest | | **Day‑3 12:45 pm** | Carve & serve | --- ## 7. Extra Tips for First‑Time Success | Tip | Why It Helps | |-----|--------------| | **Use a meat thermometer** | Guarantees doneness and safety. | | **Don’t over‑baste** | Too much moisture can keep the skin from crisping. | | **Let the bird rest** | Prevents dry meat. | | **Keep the oven door closed** | Avoids temperature fluctuations. | | **Plan for leftovers** | Store in airtight containers; reheat in the oven or microwave. | | **Ask for help** | Having a family member help with carving or side dishes can ease the pressure. | --- ## 8. Sample Family‑Recipe‑Friendly Turkey > *Feel free to adjust the quantities to match your family’s exact recipe.* **Ingredients** - 1 whole turkey (12 lb), thawed - 1 cup kosher salt - ½ cup brown sugar - 1 lb turkey (for brine) - 4 cups water (enough to cover) - 4 Tbsp unsalted butter, softened - 2 Tbsp olive oil - 4 Tbsp chopped fresh rosemary - 4 Tbsp chopped fresh thyme - 4 Tbsp chopped fresh sage - 4 cloves garlic, minced - 1 Tbsp black pepper - 1 cup chicken broth (for drip pan) **Brine (optional)** 1. Dissolve salt & sugar in water. Add turkey, herbs, and garlic. Chill 12–24 h. **Seasoning** 1. Mix butter, olive oil, herbs, garlic, pepper. 2. Rub under skin and over the surface. 3. Let sit 30 min at room temp. **Roast** 1. Preheat oven to 325 °F. 2. Place turkey on rack, add broth to drip pan. 3. Roast 3 h, basting every 45 min. 4. Check temps: 165 °F breast, 175 °F thigh. **Rest & Serve** 1. Rest 25 min. 2. Carve and serve with your family’s favorite sides. --- ### Final Thought The key to a successful first turkey is preparation and confidence. By following the timeline, using a thermometer, and honoring your family’s recipe, you’ll deliver a centerpiece that meets everyone’s expectations—and maybe even sets a new family tradition! Good luck, and enjoy the feast.
